summary: A single billing cycle includes ordinary purchases that stay under the credit limit, followed by statement closing and a full payment made before the due date. The scenario tests an on-time payoff path where the minimum payment obligation is satisfied, the purchase grace period is preserved, and neither a late fee nor an over-limit fee should be triggered.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of this billing cycle, so the grace-period condition is satisfied under clause.6b.grace_period.
The cardholder's credit limit is $1000.00, and total purchases in this cycle never cause the outstanding balance to exceed that limit.
The statement closing date is 2025-05-31 and the payment due date shown on that statement is 2025-06-25, giving at least 25 days before payment is due.
All purchases in this scenario are ordinary domestic purchase transactions, not cash advances, balance transfers, ATM withdrawals, or international transactions.
The payment made on 2025-06-20 is received and credited on the same date through an approved standard payment method.
Because the full statement balance is paid on or before the due date, this archetype expects no late payment fee, no over-limit fee, and no purchase interest for the billed purchases.
